result.evidence: (a) Refutation lands: the root Immutable identities and owned interfaces explicitly defines the seam leaf as versioned plans, state/result/error types and "inert dispatch/signatures"; ht-qhz.1 likewise says "Land only compilable additive ... inert protocol/CLI/journal dispatch wiring" and "inert-by-default ... no topology effect." That is the independently completable neutral contract the finding says is absent. Consuming the named actor-route/classifier seam specifies the agreed boundary; it does not expressly require importing unlanded peer implementation or enabling retry execution. The requirement to classify before new journal retry governs every enabled retry path, including cleanup; inert rejection until origin integration preserves it. (b) The root specifically says only actual blocking shared boundaries gate their integration leaf, and its recovery grammar requires the peer-approved dispatch before the recovery leaf is edited; ht-qhz.6 expressly gates exact human integration on peer source. Reading ht-qhz.1 as a compulsory live actor integration gate contradicts its explicitly inert scope. (c) Native ht-qhz.3 and persistence ht-qhz.2.1 depend on that genuine shared topology contract, which they consume; a separate contract bead is a possible scheduling preference, not required by the contract. (d) The alleged unrelated-work stall is therefore not entailed: neutral types/inert entry points can land first while execution stays disabled until canonical guards and original actor integration, tested by ht-qhz.5.2, ht-qhz.6 and ht-qhz.19. The independent migration0028 source gate remains explicitly limited to ht-qhz.2.1 awaiting actual0026/0027. This is an internal structural finding; no external premise is needed.
